title: TutorMoments finds AI tutors often help too much
friendlyTitle: AI tutors may help so much that students learn less
summary: Ai2 released TutorMoments, an evaluation built from 462 de-identified one-to-one maths tutoring transcripts and more than 1,500 teacher-annotated decision points. Its preview finds that models told only to tutor well tend to over-help, while explicit instructions about when to support or challenge a student improve but do not solve the problem.
friendlySummary: A new test shows that AI tutors often do too much of the work. Clear instructions help them choose when to give a hint and when to let the student think.
whyItMatters: A useful tutor should not simply produce the answer faster; it should preserve the learner’s thinking. Parents, educators and product teams can improve AI tutoring prompts by asking for questions, hints and adjustable support rather than full solutions by default.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Ask an AI tutor to guide you with questions instead of giving the full answer. The struggle to solve a problem is part of learning.
